transcript.text: It is quite common for ovens to appear dead after a power cut because the clock resets into automatic mode, which stops heating until you switch it to manual. Other possibilities include a tripped fuse at the cooker point or a simple setting issue like being on defrost rather than a heating function. Please first check if the clock display is flashing; if so, try setting the time and switching the oven to manual (often a hand symbol) to see if it powers up. Also, ensure you have turned the temperature knob up so that any indicator light comes on. Let me know if this restores power or if the appliance remains completely unresponsive.
yes its flashing 0.00 and a little symbol. i dont have the manual though, how do i set the time?

To set the time, look for a button with a clock icon or one labelled 'Clock' or 'Time'; you often need to hold it down while using the '+' and '-' buttons (or the number pad) to adjust the hours and minutes, then press 'Clock' again to save. Since I cannot confirm what "0.00" means on your specific model as it is not a standard error code for this brand, we will focus on the flashing display which usually indicates a power reset. The most likely cause of your oven not coming on right now is that it has defaulted into an automatic or timed mode after losing power, which inhibits heating until you set the time and switch to manual. Please try setting the current time using those buttons and then look for a 'Manual' button or a hand symbol to turn off any timer functions. Let me know if the oven starts working once you have done this.
